scope: Agentic latest-paper AC-WM SOTA and real-robot-demo request
summary: The round produced a reproducible data/training/evaluation framework and a structurally verified BWM action-adapter smoke checkpoint, but did not establish SOTA or execute a physical-robot demo.
evidence: Sixteen focused CPU tests, targeted Ruff, both campaign JSON validations, and the experience ledger validation pass.
A real RoboTwin Parquet smoke and the released BWM demo both load as 57-frame video with 14D robot-base actions.
The pinned official BWM/Wan runtime completed one GPU optimization step and saved a finite action-encoder-only artifact.
The promotion code fails closed until paired results beat every declared baseline on WorldArena, cross-embodiment, and at least 20 real-robot trials.
lessons: Agentic iteration is useful for exposing and correcting integration failures, but it cannot replace balanced training, frozen comparisons, or physical evidence.
Recent AC-WM research supports action alignment, embodiment holdouts, memory ablations, and causal metrics; it does not justify an unevaluated SOTA claim.
limitations: No balanced multi-embodiment training campaign or matched-seed baseline suite was run.
WorldArena, cross-embodiment, and real-robot promotion inputs remain absent.
No controllable physical robot, calibrated camera, operator approval, synchronized telemetry, safety log, or blind outcome review was available.
next_actions: Reserve uncontended GPUs and run the frozen balanced campaign against public BWM, Ctrl-World, OSCAR, Kinema4D, and required ablations.
Obtain hardware and operator access, then execute prediction-before-action physical trials under configs/acwm/real_robot_demo_protocol.json.
